newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, Lukashenko sign brief treaty on union.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, Lukashenko sign brief treaty on union.

text.p: Presidents Boris Yeltsin of Russia and Alexander Lukashenko of Belarus on Wednesday signed a brief document which will form the basis for a union between the two former Soviet republics, Itar-Tass news agency said.

The contents of the document were not immediately known. But it is expected to differ from a 17-page draft, which provided for the two states to coordinate foreign, economic and defence policies but stopped short of a merger into a single state.
The two leaders, attending a ceremony in the Moscow Kremlin, also initialled a more detailed charter on union, which will now be subject to public discussion for one month.
The decision to sign only a short accord appears to reflect a compromise reached in last-minute bargaining.

Lukashenko and the more conservative part of the Russian leadership had wanted a more binding document to be signed, including a detailed section which appears to have been transferred into the charter.

Liberals in the Russian government opposed the original draft, saying they feared union could harm Russia's economy and make Lukashenko, who once professed an admiration for Adolf Hitler, a key player in Moscow politics.
